## Documented gaps

- **hostile-time-rewound-handset-track-continuing-in-place** — 15/15 escaped. This is the residual of the replay family, and it is narrow enough to state exactly: on the mobile plane the clock gate is off, so a rewound sample is judged over the MinStepInterval floor — which accepts ANY position within `tierCeiling x MinStepInterval` of the last accepted fix. For a sedan at 180 km/h and a 1 s floor that is 50 metres. So a handset can rewind its own timeline indefinitely as long as it keeps moving plausibly, and the control that refuses it is the R-17/T-05 `seq` watermark in position-processor-svc — `seq <= last_seen_seq` is discarded — not this gate. HotPath.Tests/PositionGateTests owns that assertion; measured here so the division of labour is visible rather than assumed.
- **hostile-teleport-inside-a-backlog** — 6/6 escaped. A backlog deliberately skips the step gates: a vehicle's own history is by definition not where it is now, and judging it as a teleport would drop a whole offline buffer the moment the device reconnected (C039). What bounds pos/replay is T-05 — the 20 samples/s/device pacer in mqtt-bridge-svc and the `seq` watermark — not this gate. The per-sample gates (accuracy, satellites) do still apply, which is why a hostile backlog is not unbounded.
- **hostile-silence-then-reappearance-past-the-meta-ttl** — 4/4 escaped. VehicleMetaTtl is 10 minutes and it is also the step gate's horizon: a vehicle silent longer has no last accepted position, so its next sample is accepted unchecked. PositionProcessorOptions says so at the declaration. It is the right way round — the alternative is measuring a step over an unknown gap — but it means a spoofer who waits out the TTL relocates for free. Bounded by everything downstream that is not this gate: dispatch's 30 s tracker-freshness rule (T-11) will not offer a ride to a vehicle that has been dark for eleven minutes, and the reappearance is visible in telemetry.positions.
- **hostile-slow-walk-to-a-fabricated-location** — 40/40 escaped. A spoofer who moves the vehicle at a speed its tier allows is, to a plausibility gate, a vehicle driving. Nothing in D-18/T-07 can separate them and nothing here pretends to: the controls are elsewhere and are about identity rather than physics — mTLS device binding, the EMQX topic ACL, T-08 anti-cloning, and for a ride in progress the passenger being in the vehicle. Recorded so a reader does not mistake a green corpus for 'GPS spoofing is solved'.
